questions.text:
Which of the following languages are undecidable? Note that [latex]\left \langle M \right \rangle[/latex] indicates encoding of the Turing machine [latex]M[/latex].

[latex]L_1=\{\left \langle M \right \rangle|L(M)=\varnothing \}[/latex]
[latex]L_2=[/latex]{[latex]\left \langle M,w,q \right \rangle|M[/latex] on input w reaches state q in exactly 100 steps}
[latex]L_3=\{\left \langle M \right \rangle|L(M) \;is \; not \; recursive\}[/latex]
[latex]L_4=\{\left \langle M \right \rangle|L(M) \;contains \; at \; least\; 21 \; members\}[/latex]
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- [latex]L_1[/latex] (language is empty): non-trivial property of L(M) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] undecidable (Rice).
- [latex]L_2[/latex]: just simulate M on w for 100 steps [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] decidable.
- [latex]L_3[/latex] (L(M) not recursive): non-trivial property [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] undecidable.
- [latex]L_4[/latex] (at least 21 strings): non-trivial property [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] undecidable.

Answer: [latex]L_1,L_3[/latex] and [latex]L_4[/latex] only

questions.text:
Let A and B be two nxn matrices over real numbers. Let rank(M) and det(M) denote the rank and determinant of a matrix M, respectively. Consider the following statements.

I. rank(AB)=rank (A)rank (B)
II. det(AB)=det(A)det(B)
III. rank(A+B) [latex]\leq[/latex] rank (A) + rank (B)
IV. det(A+B) [latex]\leq[/latex] det(A) + det(B)

Which of the above statements are TRUE?
questions.solution:
Use A = B = I (n = 2):
- I: rank(AB) = 2 but rank(A)rank(B) = 4 [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.
- II: det(AB) = det(A)det(B) is always true [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- III: rank is subadditive: [latex]rank(A+B)\le rank(A)+rank(B)[/latex] [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- IV: det(2I) = 4 [latex]\gt[/latex] det(I) + det(I) = 2 [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.

Answer: II and III only

questions.text:
Consider the Boolean function [latex]z(a,b,c)[/latex].

Which one of the following minterm lists represents the circuit given above?
questions.solution:
From the circuit: [latex]z=a+\bar b c[/latex].

- a = 1: minterms 4, 5, 6, 7
- a = 0, b = 0, c = 1: minterm 1

[latex]z=\Sigma(1,4,5,6,7)[/latex]

Answer: [latex]\Sigma(1,4,5,6,7)[/latex]

questions.text:
Consider three registers R1, R2, and R3 that store numbers in IEEE-754 single precision floating point format. Assume that R1 and R2 contain the values (in hexadecimal notation) 0x42200000 and 0xC1200000, respectively.

If [latex]R3=\frac{R1}{R2}[/latex], what is the value stored in R3?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- R1 = 0x42200000: sign 0, exponent 132 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]2^5[/latex], mantissa 1.01[latex]{}_2[/latex] = 1.25 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 40
- R2 = 0xC1200000: sign 1, exponent 130 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]2^3[/latex], mantissa 1.25 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]-[/latex]10

R3 = 40 / ([latex]-[/latex]10) = [latex]-[/latex]4 = [latex]-1.0\times2^2[/latex]: sign 1, exponent 129 = 1000 0001, mantissa 0
Bits: 1100 0000 1000 0000 [latex]\ldots[/latex] = 0xC0800000

Answer: 0xC0800000

questions.text:
A computer system with a word length of 32 bits has a 16 MB byte- addressable main memory and a 64 KB, 4-way set associative cache memory with a block size of 256 bytes. Consider the following four physical addresses represented in hexadecimal notation.

A1=0x42C8A4,
A2=0x546888,
A3=0x6A289C,
A4=0x5E4880

Which one of the following is TRUE?
questions.solution:
Lines = 64 KB / 256 B = 256; sets = 256 / 4 = 64 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 6 set bits after the 8 offset bits.
Set = (address / 256) mod 64, i.e. the low 6 bits of the address without its last two hex digits:
- A1 = 0x42C8A4 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 0x42C8 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] set 8
- A2 = 0x546888 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 0x5468 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] set 40
- A3 = 0x6A289C [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 0x6A28 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] set 40
- A4 = 0x5E4880 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 0x5E48 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] set 8

A2 and A3 share set 40 (A1 and A4 share set 8).

Answer: A2 and A3 are mapped to the same cache set
